newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lower duties spark surge in S.African car imports.
newsitem.headline: Lower duties spark surge in S.African car imports.

text.p: Reduced import duties on fully built-up cars and imported components have triggered a sharp rise in the number of cars being imported to South Africa, the National Association of Automative Component and Allied Manufacturers (NAACAM) said on Thursday.
Addressing an Auto Africa conference, NAACAM president Johan Meyer said: "The result is that foreign exchange usage on imports is growing faster than the foreign exchange being earned on exports."

Meyer said that South Africa was importing about 30,000 fully built-up vehicles every year at a cost of about 1.2 billion rand, raising the motor industry's net use of foreign exchange to 11.6 billion in 1996.
"With the sharp increase in imports, local vehicle assembly is decreasing, damaging employment levels and stunting growth in the motor vehicle assembly and component industries," he said.
The South African car market currently offered more than 330 car model variants of which 120 are imports, said Meyer. Last year there were 270 models of which 60 were imported models.

New passenger car sales reached a 14-year high of 27,816 in October, up 28.4 percent year-on-year and almost 40 percent month-on-month, according to National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa (NAAMSA) out this week.
Industry officials put the leap in sales down to intense competition in the motor industry, included a much bugger range of models.
Total new passenger car sales rose to 208,483 units in the first 10 months of the year from 199,285 a year earlier.
